subject: Exhibit pricing anchor reconciliation - legal questions and proposed wording
messages:
From: Sally Chen <sally.chen@importantops.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ImportantOps Contracts <contracts@importantops.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing exhibits - anchor reconciliation request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The procurement team is working through the Order Form v3 and we noticed a few inconsistencies between Exhibit B (pricing schedule) and the primary Order Form that need legal clarification before we can sign. High-level questions:

- The Order Form references a monthly "packaging allocation" (SKU-level) while Exhibit B lists caps/floors at an annualized band. Are the caps/floors intended to apply to annualized usage only, or do you bill the floor/cap each month and true-up annually?
- There are two discount ladders: one in Exhibit B and one called out in the pricing appendix. How do those stack when a customer qualifies for both (e.g., packaging-tier + volume ladder)?
- We want an explicit carve-out for burst capacity that exceeds committed baseline during product launches — would that be charged at list or subject to a temporary cap?

I've attached our copy of the Order Form and the redlines we started (ExhibitB-ImportantOps-redlines.pdf). Can you confirm Redwood's interpretation and share proposed contract language we can circulate to our legal team?

We have procurement deadline next week (10/23) so a fast turnaround would be appreciated.

Best,
Sally
Sally Chen
Head of Procurement, ImportantOps

Attachment: IO-OrderForm-v3.pdf (order form, 4 pages)
Attachment: ExhibitB-ImportantOps-redlines.pdf (annotated exhibit)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sally Chen <sally.chen@importantops.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibits - anchor reconciliation request

Hi Sally — thanks for the clear notes and the redlines. Quick answers up front and I'll attach a clean redline for Exhibit B:

1) Caps/floors: Our intention is that the caps/floors are applied to the annualized committed volume and billing is done monthly with an annual true-up. In practice that means: monthly invoices reflect consumed units at the agreed unit price; at year-end we compare annualized usage against the committed band and true-up any delta (credits or additional charges).

2) Discount stacking: Packaging-tier discounts apply first (they're SKU-level multipliers). Volume ladder discounts in Exhibit B are applied after packaging-tier adjustments. We are open to more explicit sequencing language if ImportantOps prefers the opposite order.

3) Burst capacity: default approach is bill at the listed burst rate (higher than committed). We can add a limited temporary cap for the first quarter after go-live as a one-time accommodation.

I've attached "Redwood-ExhibitB-proposed-redline.docx" that: (a) clarifies "annualized" vs "per-billing period" language, (b) adds sequencing text for discount stacking, and (c) proposes a 90-day launch waiver for burst costs (subject to usage thresholds).

If that looks reasonable, I'll ask Legal to accept these wording edits and we can push an updated Order Form to DocuSign. Otherwise, happy to hop on a 30m call with your counsel.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-ExhibitB-proposed-redline.docx (proposed exhibit language, tracked)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: suggested clause language + commercial risk notes

Marissa / Ben / Laura — quick internal thoughts to keep legal/finance aligned before we send anything back to ImportantOps: 

- Proposed floor/cap sentence: "Caps and floors set forth in Exhibit B shall be measured on an annualized basis against the Customer's committed units. Monthly invoices are calculated on actual consumption; at the end of each 12-month period Redwood will perform a true-up and either credit or invoice the Customer for the net difference between actual usage and the annualized committed amount."

- Discount stacking: Recommend we keep packaging-tier applied first (preserves SKU-level economics) because reversing order materially changes revenue recognition and reporting. If customer pushes, we can accept alternative sequencing but should require a higher minimum commit or shorter waiver period.

- Burst carve-out: OK to offer a 90-day launch cap equal to 1.5x the committed rate for the quarter. Do NOT concede more than 1.5x without exec approval — otherwise we risk open-ended exposure.

- Billing/credit mechanics: Legal will want explicit language on timing of true-up invoices and 30-day payment term on any true-up. Finance prefers to avoid recurring credits that flow for more than two consecutive quarters.

If everyone approves, Ben can send the redline and cover note to Sally.

Karthik
VP Sales Strategy

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sally Chen <sally.chen@importantops.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibits - anchor reconciliation request

Sally — thanks for flagging these items and for the helpful redlines. We've reviewed internally and attached a single consolidated Exhibit B that implements the agreed interpretation: annualized caps/floors with monthly billing + annual true-up; packaging-tier discounts apply first, then volume ladder.

Key commercial concessions included in the attached redline:
- 90-day launch cap for burst capacity limited to 1.5x committed baseline
- True-up invoices to be issued within 30 days of the annual measurement window close
- Credits, if any, will be applied as a one-time invoice adjustment rather than recurring credits across multiple billing cycles

Please see the attached "Redwood-ExhibitB-proposed-redline.docx" (tracked). If that aligns with ImportantOps legal, we can update the order form and send to DocuSign today. Also linking the HubSpot deal for signatures: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/IO-2026-091

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-ExhibitB-proposed-redline.docx (proposal with tracked changes)

From: Sally Chen <sally.chen@importantops.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ImportantOps Contracts <contracts@importantops.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibits - anchor reconciliation request

Ben / Marissa — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clarity in the proposed wording. ImportantOps legal has two modest follow-ups before we finalize: 

1) For burst capacity, we can accept a 90-day cap, but want a cap cap (sorry) — specifically language that says Redwood will not charge more than 2.5x the committed rate for any single billing period regardless of transient spikes.
2) We need explicit language in Exhibit B that caps apply on an annualized basis "unless otherwise stated in a written amendment signed by both parties" to avoid ambiguity with future product SKUs/packaging changes.

Attached are our internal procurement notes that show why this matters for our budgeting (Internal-Procurement-Notes.docx). If you can accept the two edits above, we'll greenlight the DocuSign push and target signature by EOW.

Thanks — Sally

Attachment: Internal-Procurement-Notes.docx (internal notes, 2 pages)
